from statistics import NormalDist
Phi=NormalDist().cdf

strengths: The manuscript identifies a practically relevant privacy concern with SAM. The reported improvements in test accuracy coexist with increased membership leakage; for example, CIFAR-10 online LiRA TPR at 0.1% FPR increases from 8.8% to 12.5% while test accuracy improves from 92.3% to 93.1%.

The empirical evaluation has useful breadth: five datasets, direct threshold attacks, online and offline LiRA/RMIA, and additional optimizer and architecture comparisons. Including performance at low false-positive rates strengthens the privacy evaluation.

The memorization and influence analyses investigate an interesting explanation beyond aggregate accuracy. For the explicitly defined minimum-G-norm surrogate, the variance derivative in Lemma 4 provides a sound and interpretable mathematical observation.
weaknesses: The central theoretical model is not established as a model of SAM. Section 5 asserts that SAM induces G = I + ηΣ without deriving this correspondence. For normalized squared loss at any interpolating solution, the SAM inner maximum equals ρ²λmax(XᵀX/n)/2, independently of the interpolant. Furthermore, replacing the population covariance with the empirical Hessian in the proposed geometry leaves the Euclidean minimum-norm interpolant unchanged. Thus, the analysis does not support the claimed guarantees for SAM itself.

The likelihood-ratio guarantees have substantive mathematical problems. Lemma 11 requires v_in > v_out, which Assumption 1 does not establish, and Corollary 5 omits this condition. As a counterexample to the corollary, fixing v_in = 1 and reducing v_out from 4 to 2 decreases optimal LR advantage from approximately 0.323 to 0.166. Theorem 3 also combines an unconditional Gaussian member distribution with a conditional Gaussian non-member distribution; the unconditional non-member distribution is generally a Gaussian scale mixture.

Theorem 4 has additional proof gaps. Its comparison treats F_B as fixed, although B = −y⟨w₁,ν⟩ changes when the compared models have different w₁. Higher minority alignment alone therefore does not establish the stated accuracy ordering. Moreover, Lemma 14 infers an o_P(1) prediction fluctuation from near-orthogonality without establishing the necessary control on the learned noise-weight norm.

The proposed influence-entropy analysis needs a valid definition and a clearer comparison protocol. Equation 5 is undefined when all influences are zero and can produce invalid probabilities because influence scores are signed. Appendix H.2 assigns all-zero cases maximal entropy without resolving the normalization. It also constructs different SAM and SGD buckets with substantial non-overlap, while Figure 4 does not establish that the accuracy comparison uses identical test examples.

The evidence does not establish the claimed causal explanation through atypical subclasses. Moderate memorization scores do not independently identify informative rare patterns, and selecting the most influential examples in each interval plus illustrative images cannot establish a dataset-wide mechanism. Controlled subclass-frequency or noise experiments, independent subgroup definitions, and connections to per-example attack success would substantially strengthen this claim. The proposed variance mechanism also lacks direct empirical validation of the joint member/non-member score distributions.

The memorization comparison is insufficiently reproducible. Publicly available SGD scores are compared with newly computed SAM scores, but the manuscript does not adequately document matched training protocols, the number of models, subsampling parameters, or estimator uncertainty. These details are necessary to attribute differences specifically to the optimizer.

The attack results lack uncertainty estimates and clearly documented repetitions across independently trained target models. Averaging ten attack splits does not establish robustness to target-training randomness, particularly for the smaller reported differences. Sensitivity to SAM's perturbation radius and controls for training loss and calibration are also missing. Improved test accuracy alone does not establish a smaller loss-based generalization gap.
